history.p: The actor N.P. Nielsen wanted to recite Oehlenschläger's famous poem "Guldhornene" at a soirée at The Royal Theatre on 19 February 1832; however, he wanted it changed into a melodrama. He therefore asked C.E.F. Weyse if he was willing to undertake the task, but the latter was not interested and recommended instead his young protegé Hartmann. It became a great success which meant a turning point in Hartmann's career, being the first time he wrote music in the so-called Nordic style, which was to be a characteristic feature in many of his later works.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound with "Jurabjerget, Op. 14". In full cloth binding with handwritten label in Hartmann's hand on front cover inscribed: "Guldhornene - Op: 11 og / Jurabjergene - Op: 14, / to Melodramer til Texter af / Oehlenschlæger. - / 1832 og 1833. / Partitur." Written in brown ink with numerous emendations in red crayon. Paper: 14 staves. Paginated 1-52, starting with title page. In upper right-hand corner of the first music page (p. 3) signed and dated, which has been partly cut out due to binding. On pp. 48-52 Hartmann has added trb. and tromb. in purple ink, which indicates that it is a much later addition. At the end of the music on p. 52 end dated: "d: 30te Jan: 1832."

Bound in cardboard cover with marbled sides and leather spine. On the front cover two handwritten labels: "Hartmann / Guldhornene af Oehlenschlæger / Melodram. / Op. 11 / Partitur" and "Musikforeningens Archiv A. No 173. / Partitur / Hartmann / Guldhornene / Melodram.". Written in brown ink. Paper: 14 staves. The original text is written in Kurrent script, but a version in Latin script has later been added in pencil. Paginated in pencil 1-52. Last page blank.

Written in brown ink. Paper: 14 staves. With minor corrections and additions in Hartmann's hand. The text is in Emil Erslev's hand. On p. 11 between staves 9 and 10 Hartmann has written: "forrige Side ved [specialtegn]" which signifies that this manuscript probably was printer's copy for the first printed edition, published in 1870 by Horneman & Erslev.

annot.p: For unknown reasons the piano score has been split up in two parts: pp. 1-8 and pp. 9-12.
